summary: CCC-built 1941 steel fire tower in Sugar Hill State Forest, NY; staffed into the late 1980s. A state notice now says it is closed to the public.

facts.design: 67 ft 6 in International Derrick steel fire tower with a 1941 observer's cabin

staffing.status: no longer staffed as a lookout

access.note: NYS DEC notice on its fire towers page: currently closed to the public. A hiking guide describes climbing to the level below the cabin, with the cabin closed

visit.trail_note: Parking and trailhead at the Sugar Hill Recreation Area off Tower Hill Road, with the Six Nations trail system

facts.agency: New York State Department of Environmental Conservation

events.note: Erected by the CCC; NHLR gives a 67 ft 6 in International Derrick tower
Volunteer staffing ended in 1951 per NHLR
State staffing ended 1979 per NHLR; other sources put the end in the mid-1980s or after the 1988 season
Lookout operations ended after the 1988 season and the tower was officially closed in early 1989

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR says state staffing ended in 1979. The hiking guide says the tower was used until the mid-1980s, and Wikipedia says lookout operations ended after the 1988 season and the tower was officially closed in early 1989. The story reports all three without choosing one.

The DEC fire towers page carries a notice that the tower is currently closed to the public, and says stairs may be climbed at the user's own risk outside the cabin's season. The hiking guide describes climbing to the level below the cabin, and Wikipedia says the tower is open to the public. The DEC notice is treated as current; the undated older descriptions are not.

Wikipedia places the tower on Sproul Hill and says the Sugar Hill name comes from the reforestation area. The register and the DEC page call it the Sugar Hill Fire Tower. The brief's coordinates match Wikipedia's Sproul Hill entry.
NHLR and Wikipedia give 67 ft 6 in (20.57 m); the hiking guide gives 68 ft. The story uses 67 ft 6 in.

notes_for_editor: The DEC notice says the tower is closed; the crawl date of that page is unknown, so confirm with DEC Region 8 before publishing as current. The CNY Hiking and Wikipedia access text is undated. The NHLR credits DEC Region 8 staff with preserving the 1941 cabin, but no current cabin status was verified. The NY Almanack 2026 article (consistently staffed until the 1980s) was seen only in search and grep output and was not used as a citation.
